holidays.name: Pi Day
holidays.description: Math nerds everywhere celebrate the endlessly nonrepeating number 3.14159... by eating pie, reciting digits of pi, and making circle-themed puns. The date works because March 14 is 3/14, matching the first three digits of pi.
holidays.origin: Physicist Larry Shaw organized the first Pi Day in 1988 at the San Francisco Exploratorium. Staff and visitors marched in a circle and ate fruit pies. The U.S. House of Representatives made it an official observance in 2009. UNESCO later proclaimed March 14 the International Day of Mathematics.
holidays.funFact: The first Pi Day included a march around a circular space in the Exploratorium. Pi Day also falls on Albert Einstein's birthday, March 14, 1879.

holidays.name: National Potato Chip Day
holidays.description: A salute to the crispy, salty snack that has launched a million bags and ruined a million diets. Crunch into your favorite flavor, from classic salted to something wild like dill pickle.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. Its origin is unclear, but it is celebrated each year on March 14 by snack lovers.
holidays.funFact: A popular legend credits chef George Crum with inventing the potato chip in 1853 in Saratoga Springs, New York. He supposedly sliced potatoes paper-thin to annoy a customer who kept sending his fries back. The story is widely repeated, but food historians doubt it, since chip-like recipes appeared in print earlier.

holidays.name: Learn About Butterflies Day
holidays.description: A day to flutter into the world of butterflies. You can learn how they transform from caterpillars, plant nectar flowers for them, or just spot a few as spring begins.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is timed to the arrival of spring, when butterflies begin to emerge.
holidays.funFact: Butterflies taste with their feet. Sensors on their legs let them sample a leaf as soon as they land on it.
